correctness.rationale: Lewko's finite two-ordering ingredients provide a bad \(m\)-term trigonometric block and a permutation \(\sigma\) forcing the prescribed arithmetic-progression order inside either \(	au\) or \(\sigma\circ	au\). Sampling the open bad set on sufficiently fine prime cyclic groups preserves a fixed positive density. The block matrix with columns \(u_n\) and \(v_n\) is exactly orthonormal on \(2M\) atoms by cyclic-character orthogonality and the layer sign; all entries are \(2M\)-th roots. Restricting any full column ordering to the distinguished \(u\)-columns and assigning zeros elsewhere preserves the relevant partial sums, while primeness makes the progression step a permutation of the grid. This establishes the finite complete Butson basis claim.
residual_risks: The proof is existential and gives no useful \(M_0(H)\).

evidence: Both broader sources allow general finite systems; neither checked statement forces the complete \(2M\)-vector basis on \(2M\) atoms with root-of-unity entries.
